guideTitle: 6 Best Portable Wheelchair Ramps Under $100 in 2026
metaDescription: Six folding aluminum wheelchair ramps in two-foot and three-foot lengths for low steps and curbs, compared on rise range, rated load, weight, and setup.
introParagraphs: At this budget, portable wheelchair ramps are short suitcase-style folding aluminum panels meant for one low step, a curb cut, or a raised doorway. They are not permanent entrances, and they are not meant for a full flight of stairs. What you are really choosing is a length and a stated rise range that fit the exact height you measured.

We evaluated six picks, three at two feet and three at three feet, based on product specs and buyer feedback. We compared stated rise ranges, load ratings, folded and open dimensions, listed weight, and surface treatment. Every product is listed at or under the cap, so the useful question is how much of your rise each length can handle without becoming steep.

A reminder before you read further. The common rule of thumb is a 1:12 slope, which means one inch of rise needs twelve inches of ramp, so a short ramp is only comfortable on a very low step. Always check your mobility device's owner guide for incline limits, and ask an occupational therapist if you are unsure how steep a crossing can safely be for the person using it.

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 3FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.description:
HYUNAN METHOD publishes the complete numbers for this three-foot ramp. It opens to 36 by 29 by 2.4 inches, folds to 36 by 14.5 by 3.2 inches, and weighs 14.02 lb. The maker states an 800 lb capacity, a rise range of 3 to 9 inches, and includes guardrails and reflective strips.

The top of that range deserves caution. A 9 inch rise over 3 feet is a 1:4 slope, far steeper than the 1:12 rule of thumb, and the sensible use is near the bottom of the range. The listing also does not describe the surface material in the text reviewed. The maker advises that if you are in doubt, you should go to the next longer ramp.

Compared with the VEVOR three-foot ramp, which states 3 to 6 inches, this one claims a wider window but invites the steepest use. At 14.02 lb it is lighter than a typical door but heavier than the two-foot Rocspire at 9.5 lb. Use the numbers as a boundary, not a target. For a single step of about 3 inches, this ramp gives a gentle 1:12 slope and a published weight.

products.name: VEVOR 3FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp, 800 LB
products.description:
VEVOR sells a three-foot folding ramp rated by the maker for 3 to 6 inch door, garage, and driveway curbs, with an 800 lb capacity. The surface is grooved aluminum with a full-coverage non-slip coating. Raised side baffles help keep wheels on the ramp, and reflective strips add visibility after dark.

A narrower stated range is a more cautious claim than HYUNAN's 3 to 9 inches. The listing does not provide folded dimensions or weight in the text reviewed, which makes it harder to plan storage. A 6 inch rise over 3 feet is a 1:6 slope, still steep for a self-propelled chair.

Among the three-foot picks, it shares the 800 lb rating of Support Way and HYUNAN but gives less size data than HYUNAN. The coated, grooved surface is a clear differentiator from simply frosted aluminum. If your step is about 3 inches, you will get a gentle slope. Measure the exact rise at the spot and match it to the stated range, not the other way round.
products.bestFor: Door and garage curbs of 3 to 6 inches with side baffles for guidance.

products.name: Support Way 3FT Folding Wheelchair Ramp, 800 lbs
products.description:
Support Way describes a three-foot folding ramp that unfolds and locks in seconds with no tools. The surface is toothed aluminum described as grippy in any weather, and the stated capacity is 800 lb. The maker sizes it for porch steps and thresholds up to 5 inches, with 3 inches as the guide for solo use.

That honest split between solo and helper use is useful. A 5 inch rise over 3 feet is about 1:7, and the maker suggests a helper above 3 inches. The listing does not give weight or folded size in the text reviewed, so check them before relying on it.

Compared with HYUNAN and VEVOR, it narrows the usable range but makes the helper limit explicit. It also has the quickest setup claim among the three-foot ramps. For a caregiver who opens it several times a day, that matters. A solo user with a 3 inch step gets the intended 1:12 slope, which is the one to aim for. Practice unfolding and locking it before the first real crossing.

products.name: Rocspire 2FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp, 800lb
products.description:
Rocspire's two-foot ramp opens to 24 by 29 by 2 inches and folds to 24 by 14 by 2.8 inches. The maker states a 2 to 6 inch rise range, an 800 lb rating, and a weight of 9.5 lb, the lightest published figure in this group. Stainless steel hinges resist rust, and rubber pads at the base help resist sliding.

The top of the range is a 1:4 slope on only 24 inches, which is steep, so treat 2 inches as the comfortable end. The textured frosted surface can wear with heavy use, and the description does not name the exact material. Two very low steps in total would exceed the stated limit.

It is the two-foot ramp with the clearest numbers, ahead of FACHNUO and VNN on rating. The 9.5 lb weight is about 4.5 lb less than the HYUNAN three-footer. For a single curb or a threshold of 2 inches, the slope is near 1:12. Wipe the rubber pads clean so the ramp keeps its grip on the ground.

products.name: FACHNUO 2FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp for Home Steps
products.description:
FACHNUO lists its two-foot ramp at 24 by 29.2 by 2 inches open and 24 by 13.2 by 3.2 inches folded, with a weight of 10.9 lb. The surface is textured, non-slip aluminum, and the sides have baffles and reflective strips for low-light visibility. Guide rails extend along the edges to help keep wheels on the ramp.

A short run steepens quickly above 3 inches, and the listing does not suit full steps or porches. The text does not give a rated capacity in the part reviewed, so a heavy user and device should confirm it first. It is a threshold and curb ramp, not a stair solution.

It weighs 1.4 lb more than the Rocspire two-footer and states no capacity, while Rocspire gives 800 lb. Its folded width of 13.2 inches is the slimmest of the group. It suits a car trunk or a closet. Open it fully, confirm that it locks, and check the ground contact before every use.

products.name: VNN 2FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp for Home Steps
products.description:
VNN offers a two-foot aluminum ramp sized at 24 by 28.2 inches, for step heights from 2 to 6 inches. Transition plates ease the step edge, and bottom pads help hold the ramp in place. The surface has folds that increase friction and an extra coating meant for wet conditions.

Its 600 lb rating is the lowest in the group, so add up the user and the device carefully. The 6 inch limit is strict, and the text does not give weight or folded size. The listing also asks you to read its buyer guide before purchase, which is good practice.

Where Rocspire and FACHNUO sit at 800 lb or unstated, this one has a lower stated rating but includes transition plates. The plates reduce the lip where the ramp meets the step. For a lighter combined load and a single low step, it is adequate. A 6 inch step over 2 feet is a 1:4 slope, so use the lower end of its range for comfort.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Measure from the ground to the top of the surface the ramp will rest on, including any threshold lip. Underestimating by an inch steepens the slope more than you expect. A 3 inch rise on the three-foot HYUNAN or Support Way gives about 1:12, while the same rise on the VNN two-foot is 1:8. When you fall between lengths, choose the longer ramp.

The 1:12 rule means one inch of rise needs twelve inches of ramp. A 6 inch rise on a 3 foot VEVOR is 1:6, and on a 2 foot Rocspire it is 1:4. Two feet suits 2 inches, three feet suits 3 inches. The stated maximums, such as HYUNAN's 9 inches, describe what the ramp can physically bridge, not what is comfortable.

The rating must exceed user plus chair or scooter plus carried items. HYUNAN, VEVOR, Support Way, and Rocspire state 800 lb, while VNN states 600 lb and FACHNUO gives none in the text reviewed. Check the device owner guide for incline limits too. A high rating does not make a steep slope any easier.

A ramp you cannot lift will stay in the garage. Rocspire lists 9.5 lb, FACHNUO 10.9 lb, and HYUNAN 14.02 lb. Support Way, VEVOR, and VNN give no weight in the text reviewed. Folded size matters too, since FACHNUO is 24 by 13.2 inches and HYUNAN is 36 by 14.5 inches. Try lifting and folding it before you rely on it.

Textured aluminum helps in wet weather. VEVOR adds a non-slip coating over grooves, Support Way has a toothed surface, and Rocspire has frosted aluminum with rubber pads. Side baffles on VEVOR and FACHNUO help keep wheels on the ramp. Keep the surface clear of leaves, ice, and grit.

These ramps are portable aids, not code-compliant permanent entrances. A permanent entry may need landings, handrails, and permits. Folding ramps also trade portability for seams. Use them for occasional crossings and ask an occupational therapist about a more permanent solution if the need is daily.

howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the stated rise ranges with the ramp length to see which can offer a gentle slope. Support Way and HYUNAN suit about 3 inches at 3 feet, while Rocspire suits about 2 inches at 2 feet. Maximum ranges were treated as limits, not recommendations.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rated load transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on product specs and buyer feedback, we noted which listings give a capacity. HYUNAN, VEVOR, Support Way, and Rocspire state 800 lb, VNN states 600 lb, and FACHNUO gives none in the text reviewed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stated weight and folded size. Rocspire at 9.5 lb leads, FACHNUO has the slimmest fold, and HYUNAN publishes the most complete set of numbers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Surface and guidance features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared textures, coatings, baffles, rails, and reflective strips. VEVOR combines grooves and coating, and FACHNUO and HYUNAN include reflective strips. VNN adds transition plates.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every pick is at or under the cap, so we asked which gives the most dependable information for a single low step. HYUNAN leads on data, Support Way on setup speed, and Rocspire on the two-foot class.

faq.q: How long should my ramp be for a 3 inch step?
faq.a: The 1:12 rule says 3 inches of rise needs about 36 inches of ramp, so a three-foot model such as Support Way or HYUNAN is the natural fit. A two-foot ramp would be 1:8, which is steeper. If you are between lengths, go to the longer one.

faq.q: Are the maximum rise numbers safe to use?
faq.a: They show what the ramp can physically bridge, not a comfortable slope. HYUNAN's 9 inches on 3 feet is 1:4. Treat the low end of each range as the practical target and check your device's incline limit.

faq.q: What does the 800 lb rating mean?
faq.a: It is the maker's stated capacity for the ramp. Add the user, the chair or scooter, and anything carried. Most listings here say 800 lb, VNN says 600 lb, and FACHNUO does not give a figure in the text reviewed. A higher number does not change the slope.

faq.q: Can I leave a portable ramp in place permanently?
faq.a: These ramps are meant for occasional use, not as code-compliant permanent entrances. A permanent ramp may need landings, handrails, and permits. Ask a local authority or an occupational therapist.

faq.q: Do side baffles and rails prevent falls?
faq.a: They help guide wheels, but no listing promises injury prevention. VEVOR and FACHNUO include side features. Stay in the center, move slowly, and use help when needed.

faq.q: How do I keep the ramp from sliding?
faq.a: Place it on a clean, flat surface and use the rubber pads or bottom pads that come with Rocspire and VNN. Check that both ends sit flat and the hinges are locked before use.

faq.q: Who can advise on the right slope?
faq.a: An occupational therapist or physical therapist can match slope to the person and device. Also read the owner guide of the chair or scooter for incline limits. Share your measured rise with them.
